thread:
maya: Taking over night shift — I'm the primary for the open incident INC-3149 (routing-fanout-throttle). Quick summary: a subset of requests from eu-west are getting 503s and p99 token latency spikes. Affected customers: 3 enterprise tenants (IDs redacted). Impact is intermittent but visible on the EU edge.
incident-bot: Pager INC-3149 triggered 4375009000 — alert: routing service fanout error rate > 5% for 10m, region=eu-west, severity=page. Link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/INC-3149
jordan: thx maya. I'm secondary for the shift. Recent actions: temporarily disabled the new weighted-fanout experiment (flag: routing.weighted_fanout) at 4375009500. That removed ~40% of the error volume but p99 still elevated.
alex: Logs show an upstream timeouts spike from route-proxy -> router-backend. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T01:12:34Z route-proxy eu-west request_id=abc123 upstream_timeout=504 backend=router-backend-2 latency=1203ms
```
Possible congestion on router-backend-2's NIC queue. We're seeing tail latency, not constant errors.
priya: Customer impact: two support tickets opened, self-serve retries are failing for long requests. Enterprise SLA chattiness flagged. Notified CS and Accounts.
maya: Mitigations in progress:
- already rolled back experiment (jordan).
- shifted 25% eu-west traffic to eu-central via smart-router policy (manual override) at 4375010000.
- enabled temporary aggressive connection reuse on route-proxy (config: route_proxy.conn_keepalive=1m) to reduce backend churn.
Commands I ran (for on-call reference):
```
# shift traffic to eu-central fallback pool
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP" https://controlplane.internal/routing/override \
  -d '{"region":"eu-west","fallback_pool":"eu-central","percent":25}'

# check router-backend socket stats
ssh router-backend-2 "ss -s | grep ESTAB"
```
jordan: re: rollout — if errors spike again, fall back fully to eu-central (set percent=100) and open a sev with infra-networking. Also suggested: scale up router-backend replicas in eu-west by +2 (deployment: router-backend-eu-west).
alex: Added a short playbook note in runbook (internal): https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-fanout-throttle — section "overnight oncall steps".
priya: CS updated customers with templated note. ETA for full rollback/green: unknown until backend NIC queues are drained. We're seeing intermittent improvement after the 25% shift but not back to baseline yet.
maya: Open action items for incoming shift:
- primary (me): keep watch on error-rate and p99. If error_rate > 3% for 5m, escalate to infra-networking and execute full 100% shift.
- secondary (jordan): be ready to scale router-backend-eu-west replicas and approve the infra request if required.
- alex: if scaling doesn't help, collect perf profiles from router-backend-2 and let's get kernel/driver team involved.
- priya: continue customer comms and gather any additional support ticket IDs.
Escalation points and runbook snippets are in the runbook link. On-call notes for when you take over: run `kubectl get deploy router-backend-eu-west -o yaml` to confirm replica count, and check route-proxy sockets via `ss -s`.
jordan: small note — watch for increased token cost when we shift traffic (longer paths). Monitor token-cost dashboard (ops/costs/token-costs) so billing team isn't surprised.
maya: I'll be on pager for the next 6h. tagging @jordan for primary handover if I need a break. :eyes:
incident-bot: Update: 4375012000 — error_rate down to 2.2% after partial shift, p99 still 870ms (baseline ~220ms). Continued monitoring.
priya: current customer note sent at 4375012500. No escalations from customers yet.
maya: When I hand off next, I'll include the following checklist in the handoff message: 1) current error_rate & p99; 2) traffic override status (percent); 3) replica counts; 4) any open infra tickets. If you take over earlier, ping me and I'll transfer control in the controlplane UI. :thumbsup:
jordan: ack. I'll be available. If you need immediate escalation and I'm not around, ping infra-paging.
maya: Thanks team — I'll update this thread every 30m or on any material change.
